=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text tfirst "first 15: "
text tat " first appears at "
text tgcd "gcd of each consecutive pair of the first 1000 is 1: "
text tyes "yes"
text tno "no"
global sb ulong 1200
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note start 1, 1; for each k from 1 on, append sb[k] + sb[k-1] and then sb[k], until 1200 members
fn build to void
put sb 0 1
put sb 1 1
n = ulong 2
k = ulong 1
note each pass adds two members, so 600 passes fill 1200
while lt n 1200 bound 600
put sb n add get sb k get sb sub k 1
put sb add n 1 get sb k
n = add n 2
k = add k 1
end
end
note find gives the 1-based position of v's first appearance, 0 if not within the 1200
fn find v ulong to ulong
for i ulong 1200
if eq get sb i v
ret add i 1
end
end
ret 0
end
fn gcd a ulong b ulong to ulong
note Euclid's remainders shrink at least as fast as Fibonacci numbers, so 100 steps cover any ulong
while ne b 0 bound 100
t = rem a b
a = b
b = t
end
ret a
end
fn show v ulong to void
emitu v
emit tat
emitu find v
emit nl
end
fn main to int
build
emit tfirst
for i ulong 15
if gt i 0
emit sp
end
emitu get sb i
end
emit nl
for i ulong 10
show add i 1
end
show 100
ok = true
for i ulong 999
if ne gcd get sb i get sb add i 1 1
ok = false
end
end
emit tgcd
if ok
emit tyes
else
emit tno
end
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
first 15: 1 1 2 1 3 2 3 1 4 3 5 2 5 3 4
1 first appears at 1
2 first appears at 3
3 first appears at 5
4 first appears at 9
5 first appears at 11
6 first appears at 33
7 first appears at 19
8 first appears at 21
9 first appears at 35
10 first appears at 39
100 first appears at 1179
gcd of each consecutive pair of the first 1000 is 1: yes
</pre>
